newsitem.title: USA: EEOC intervenes in Home Depot suit.
newsitem.headline: EEOC intervenes in Home Depot suit.

text.p: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission said on Monday it has moved to intervene in a private sex discrimination suit filed against do-it-yourself retailing giant Home Depot Inc.

The suit, which was filed in 1995 in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana, focuses on 310 stores east of the Mississippi. The EEOC said this was the largest private sex discrimination case in which it has sought to intervene.
The EEOC alleges that women were hired only at low level positions with no opportunities for advancement.
C. Gregory Stewart, general counsel of the EEOC, alleged that "while Home Depot has a glass ceiling, Home Depot traps its female employees into what amounts to a glass basement with glass walls."
He charged that women were hired for jobs such as cashier, but they were not hired or considered for promotion for other positions, such as sales or managerial positions.

He said the suit was one of three pending against Atlanta-based Home Depot, whose roughly 50 stores sell building materials and home improvement products in the United States and Canada. Stewart said the EEOC would assist the private lawyers in every aspect of litigation in the Louisiana case.
Home Depot's stock was 25 cents higher at $57.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
